articles.headline: Huawei has designed probably the best-looking Wi-Fi router ever, one that doesn't look like an 8-legged spider and costs less than $100
keyFacts: Huawei introduced the Router X2 Pro, a wireless networking device featuring a book-inspired enclosure and interchangeable magnetic covers.
The device supports Wi-Fi 7+, mesh networking, and integrated technologies designed to improve signal transmission and reduce lag.
A single unit of the router sells for 588 yuan, which is approximately 88 US dollars.
body: - Huawei's new router replaces conventional styling with a book-inspired enclosure
- The Router X2 Pro supports Wi-Fi 7+ wireless networking technology
- Magnetic covers allow users to customize the router's external appearance
Huawei has introduced the Router X2 Pro, a wireless networking device with a book-inspired design that departs from conventional router appearances.
The new model combines Wi-Fi 7+ technology with mesh Wi-Fi and a decorative enclosure, allowing it to function as part of a home's interior rather than simply networking equipment.
It also supports interchangeable magnetic covers, four integrated Wi-Fi antennas and several networking technologies intended to improve wireless performance.
A router designed to look like a book
Unlike routers built around exposed antennas and angular plastic housings, Huawei's latest model uses a rectangular enclosure resembling a closed book.
Its measurements are 191.7 × 51.1 × 141.1mm, while the complete unit weighs 475g, making it relatively compact for household placement.
A magnetic panel fitted along the side can also be replaced with alternative covers, including customised designs produced via three-dimensional printing.
These decorative designs feature pandas, cats, dogs and penguins, but there is no confirmation that they come with the device.

The Router X2 Pro uses four integrated Wi-Fi antennas, alongside dedicated components supporting smart antenna functions, Bluetooth and Strobe connectivity.
A separate indicator communicates the system's operating condition and Mesh networking status, providing a visible reference for the router's current state.
Connectivity features, smart networking and pricing
This Wi-Fi router uses Huawei's Lingxiao 760 series chipset alongside four high-performance signal amplifiers designed to strengthen wireless signal transmission.
It also includes dynamic narrowband technology, which improves transmission speeds and signal penetration and reduces lag by up to 80%.
These technologies help to maintain reception when signals must pass through several walls and other obstacles.
In addition, the Router X2 Pro supports NearLink technology, which improves network stability by 50%.
According to Huawei, the hardware and software combination reduces compatibility losses and supports faster video loading, responsive gaming and consistent connections.
The router supports wired connections and wireless Mesh arrangements, allowing households to select an installation method suited to their existing network.
Its AI Mesh system can analyse an uploaded home floor plan through Huawei's Smart Life application and recommend suitable equipment placement.
Additional Mesh Lights allow users to inspect connection strength, while automatic roaming manages movement between the 2.4GHz and 5GHz frequency bands.
The system monitors reception conditions and switches between available bands, while NearLink, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi provide three supported connection methods.
A unit of this device sells at 588 yuan (~ $88), while customers seeking two units can purchase the combined package for 1,108 yuan (~ $166).
The decorative casing option costs 99 yuan (~ $15), although the announcement does not clarify whether every customised cover carries that price.
The available finishes include Earthy Brown, Oak White, Stone Gray and Spruce Green, giving buyers several options for matching different interior arrangements.

articles.headline: Sunderland v Dinamo Zagreb, Celtic v Besiktas: Europa League – live
keyFacts: Daichi Kamada scored a stoppage-time goal to secure a 1-1 draw for Crystal Palace against Hoffenheim.
Bournemouth achieved a victory against Sparta Prague after overcoming a deficit and benefiting from a red card.
Ajax secured a 6-1 lead against Midtjylland in a match delayed by floodlight failure.
body: Getafe 0-0 Brighton: Hinshelwood tries to curl one in from 20 yards - the shot is going harmlessly wide until the goalkeeper decides to turn it behind regardless.

Sunderland 0-0 Dinamo Zagreb: Rigg swings in a very dangerous cross from the right for teammates to attack. It reaches Ahoka but his header is a poor one from close range and the keeper saves. It should do better.
Sunderland 0-0 Dinamo Zagreb: The Black Cats need to defend a corner from the right. It is played short and then out to around 30 yards from goal from where a shot is lashed high into the stands.
Getafe 0-0 Brighton: The Spanish side like a cross into the box, the latest concluding with a clash of heads at the back post. Costinha is able to get up and walk off.
With the 8pm kick-offs about to get under way I’m going to hand over to Will Unwin. But I have a farewell gift, in the shape of Paul MacInnes’ report on Crystal Palace 1-1 Hoffenheim. Bye!
A late, late strike from Daichi Kamada saved Crystal Palace from embarrassment and another round of navel gazing as they snatched a Europa League draw with Hoffenheim against the odds.

After being outplayed by a side currently in the bottom half of the Bundesliga, and a goal down since the seventh minute, Palace looked to have lost all hope in this fixture after Adam Wharton was dismissed with 13 minutes to go. But after Hoffenheim failed to clear a goalmouth scramble in added time, Kamada fired home under the keeper to generate a rare moment of elation at Selhurst Park this season.

Only one of the early kick-offs is still ongoing, and it’s turned into a goalfest at Midtjylland, where kick-off was delayed by a floodlight failure. It was 1-1 when Kjell Watjen was sent off in the 43rd minute, but as they approach stoppage time Ajax lead 6-1.

And it’s equally all over at Stardion Letna, where a red card brandished within a couple of minutes of Sparta Prague taking the lead in the first half changed the game, and Bournemouth eventually cantered to maximal point-accumulation.

And, in the end, Bournemouth are coasting to victory! Evanilson, scorer of the second, is creator of the third, with Rayan the scorer. And if that reads like I haven’t actually seen the goal, that impression would be accurate.
Crystal Palace rescue a point (probably) in stoppage time! A deep cross from the right is headed back across the area to Daichi Kamada, whose first-time shot deflects past Baumann!
Hoffenheim should probably also have gone down to 10 men at Selhurst Park, but the referee failed to spot Andrej Kramaric, already booked, very deliberately use his arm to control the ball.

Bournemouth have turned it around against 10-man Sparta! It’s good pressing to repeatedly get in the way of Sparta’s attempts to play the ball out and eventually they take control of it and play it to Evanilson, who’s ice-cool finish has minimal force but maximum precision!
On commentary, Glenn Hoddle gushes that Crystal Palace “have footballed their way back into this game”. Which sounds super, though there is still the small matter of the scoreline still to deal with.
The crowd microphones at Thun are picking up some very extreme displeasure from visiting supporters, of the kind that really shouldn’t be broadcast at this hour.

Surely it’s all over now! It’s not a great cross from the left but Dursun flings out a leg, gets a big toe on the ball from the edge of the six-yard box, and Beau Reus can’t react as it flies inside the near post!

Bournemouth equalise against 10-man Sparta! And poor Mbe Soh gives the ball away twice in a few seconds to set it up! The first comes as Sparta pass the ball around the defence and he finds someone in the wrong shirt entirely. He gets back in time to prevent a shot but in doing so sends the ball rolling to Tyler Adams, a half-time substitute, who slams it into the bottom corner!

At Stadion Rajko Mitic Inter d’Escaldes’ Domi Berlanga has made it 10-10 by also getting sent off, for a second yellow card, matching Red Star’s Aleksandar Katai, who received a straight red way back in the 35th minute. More importantly, it’s 0-0 in goals.
For every upstart-success story in this game, there’s a how-the-mighty-have-fallen tale. Talking of which, Marc Gual has romped through a rag-bag defence to put Kairat Almaty 1-0 up at Atalanta.

Hoffenheim remain 1-0 up at Palace, in search of their first ever victory over an English side. “Hoffenheim is quite an interesting team,” writes Rebecca Voss. “They’re not popular in Germany because their rise to the Bundesliga shouldn’t have been possible. Hoffenheim town has only three thousand people, give or take, and the club was playing in the eighth league in the 90s. However, a software mogul named Dietmar Hopp was born and raised in Hoffenheim and decided to use some of his money to help his boyhood team. He bought them in 2000, by which time Hoffenheim were in the fifth tier, and immediately Hoffenheim started to become pretty good. They were promoted to the Bundesliga in 2008 after Hopp brought in Ralf Ragnick as manager and some experienced Bundesliga players to lead the team, and they’ve been there ever since. Because of this, German media likes to claim that the club doesn’t have much of a culture or a fanbase. Hoffenheim are currently 12th in the Bundesliga and many Germans are praying for their downfall.”
For more about the genesis of this Hoffenheim side see these articles, 18 and 10 years old respectively:
Having spent an hour or so wondering why the Midtjylland v Ajax game was running so late, I have used my investigative journalist skills to locate an answer.
It’s half-time now at Thun, where the firework smoke that forced the game to be paused for a few minutes seems to have settled between the ears of the Hearts defenders. 2-0 to the home team there.

articles.headline: USMNT's Gold Cup path to look different as Concacaf unveils revamped group-stage format
keyFacts: Concacaf announced a new 2027 Gold Cup format featuring two groups of eight teams instead of four groups of four.
The tournament will run from June 17 to July 11 and includes 15 qualifying teams plus guest nation Saudi Arabia.
Concacaf president Victor Montagliani stated the change aims to create more competitive matchups and excitement throughout the group stage.
body: For the United States men's national team to win their first Concacaf Gold Cup since 2021, they'll now need to contend with a new format in the 2027 edition. The tournament will run from June 17 through July 11, with major changes coming to the group stage. It will still include only 16 teams, but instead of those teams being split into four groups of four teams each, they'll now be split into only two eight-team groups. Fifteen of those teams will qualify via the Gold Cup preliminary round and join guest nation Saudi Arabia in the tournament.

That shift has the goal of making the group stage more exciting, as not only does it add an extra game due to each team playing four teams instead of three, but it also allows a chance for chaos, as four teams will go through to the knockouts from each group. While the new game is added, that won't change how the knockouts look, as those will proceed as normal.

"The Gold Cup is our region's premier men's national team competition, and we are really excited about what this new format will bring to the tournament's Group Stage," said Concacaf president and FIFA vice president Victor Montagliani. "Our fans want to see the best teams in our region compete against each other, and this format will create more opportunities for those matchups to happen earlier in the competition. At the same time, every match will matter, with teams facing a balanced mix of opponents and competing for a place in the knockout rounds. We believe this will make for a more competitive and exciting Gold Cup from the very first match through to the Final."
Group stage format

How matchups are determined is where things get a little confusing, as they will organize the eight teams into ranking bands of two teams each, with a predetermined fixture matrix ensuring that each team plays a balanced schedule of opponents.

This is to prevent a situation where two strong Concacaf sides essentially ensure that others don't have a chance to advance, which could lead to more interesting fixtures in the knockout stages depending on how it goes.
Knockout stage format

For the knockouts, nothing changes from how things used to look, as those four teams advancing from each group will then be placed into a single bracket, with the highest-finishing teams in each group facing off against the lower-finishing teams in the opposite group. There will then be no reseeding as the quarterfinals will determine the semifinal pairings in the road to the championship.
Key dates
- Gold Cup draw: April 8
- Gold Cup kickoff: June 17
- Quarterfinals: July 3 and 4
- Semifinals: July 7 and 8
- Final: July 11

articles.headline: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 9
keyFacts: Hayden Winks released his Week 9 fantasy football wide receiver rankings and analysis for Yahoo Sports.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba is ranked as the top wide receiver for Week 9 with a projection of 92.5 receiving yards.
The column provides weekly rankings, film notes, and charts to assist fantasy football managers in building their lineups.
body: The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column , this WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions . You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available .
1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (vs. ARI) - 92.5 proj. receiving yards

JSN has 19.3 half PPR points or more in all but one game, as the clear-cut WR1 overall in fantasy. He's had big games with Drew Lock before, including in Week 2 against these Cardinals, when he had 38.0 half PPR points on 155 yards and three scores.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)
2. Puka Nacua (at WAS) - 92.5 proj. receiving yards

The Rams offense has really changed recently. In two games without Davante Adams, Nacua's average depth of target is just 3.4 yards downfield. Everything is shallow. It's fine in fantasy because he will rack up catches with ease, and he can power through tackles for first downs. But it does make it a bit harder for the offense to be a threat for 35+ points like they were in previous versions. Nacua is the WR3 on WR1 usage and has a 34% target share since returning to the lineup in Week 4. He's up to 41% targets (!!!) without Adams.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The Commanders have allowed the seventh-most passing yards per game with one of the most underwhelming CB rooms. They'll muck things up in a Diet Coke version of the Brian Flores defense, but that fits with the Rams' quick-hitting approach on offense right now. Los Angeles enters as 5.5-point road favorites with a 26.5-point team total (eighth).
3. CeeDee Lamb (at IND) - 81.5 proj. receiving yards
4. Ja'Marr Chase (at ATL) - 78.5 proj. receiving yards
Chase is the WR4 on WR9 usage if we remove his Week 4 injury game. Nothing has changed with this offense, aside from now having one of the best RTs in the NFL, Amarius Mims.
5. Tee Higgins (at ATL) - 77.5 proj. receiving yards

Higgins is the WR4 on WR13 usage this season. He's been the WR1, WR2, WR71, WR7, WR8, WR19 and WR39 this season. The Bengals abandoned their under-center pass game officially and will let Joe Burrow cook as he's done since LSU.
On targets between 10-20 air yards:
1. Tee Higgins (460 receiving yards)
2. Drake London (314) https://t.co/kapcp5AC5b
— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 2, 2026
6. Drake London (vs. CIN) - 78.5 proj. receiving yards

Last week's Penix outing was concerning because of his poor decision-making, but the conditions won't ever be that bad again. It's not a complete throw-out-the-window game, but it's close to it. Before that, London had been averaging fantasy WR1 numbers with Penix dating back to late 2024.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The matchup with the Bengals is pass-first, especially with star CB1 DJ Turner (ankle) not practicing. Cincy's LB play has been amongst the worst in the NFL, and London can hammer teams on quick in cuts, something the Falcons have leaned on more recently. It's a great matchup for London, with Atlanta projected to lose while still owning a quality 24.75-point team total (eighth).
7. Amon-Ra St. Brown (at MIA) - 76.5 proj. receiving yards
8. Malik Nabers (at PHI) - 73.5 proj. receiving yards
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)
9. Chris Olave (vs. CLE) - 71.5 proj. receiving yards
10. Justin Jefferson (vs. BUF) - 77.5 proj. receiving yards

I broke down the Vikings’ pass game in detail in another column , but it really comes down to Kyler Murray, Kevin O'Connell and Jordan Addison splitting a lot of the blame for Jefferson's falloff. Over his past 17 games, he's averaging just 50 YPG. It was at 96 YPG before them. This year, Jefferson is the WR18 on WR31 usage, while seeing a lot of bracket coverage. The Lions played outside leverage at CB with a safety on the inside for a lot of the game, and Jefferson was left unprotected from it by the staff. A few inaccuracies and turn-downs from Kyler played into a mediocre game in a great matchup. That said, Jefferson still had a huge red-zone catch, was thrown the ball underneath and Murray's stats are at a career low point. They would likely to get better with more time on task, but now Murray is week-to-week with a hamstring injury. Carson Wentz will start on MNF. I don't know if the Vikings' No. 25 neutral pass rate will change, however. Jefferson is clearly more of a fantasy WR2 than WR1.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

He draws an exploitable matchup against a Bills defense that ranks fourth in half PPR points allowed per game to opposing WR rooms (31.1). Buffalo allowed 29.2 points to Puka Nacua and 24.2 points to Tre Tucker in recent weeks. The Vikings are 3.5-point home underdogs carrying an implied team total of 21.5 points (19th).
11. Christian Watson (at NE) - 73.5 proj. receiving yards
12. Nico Collins (at LAC) - 68.5 proj. receiving yards

Collins ranks as the WR19 in per-game half PPR scoring on WR30 expected-points usage over his past four appearances. His recent stretch was keyed by a Week 4 masterclass against Dallas (WR3 overall), but it's tailed off since then while the Texans have limited his snap counts with more help in the offense. Over this 4-game sample, he has averaged 6.3 targets and 79.0 air yards on a 21% target share. It boggles the mind that this isn't higher. Hopefully the bye week was enough time for them to figure some things out — like spamming targets to him.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The Chargers rank 17th in half PPR points allowed to wide receivers at 25.3 per game. While they have been vulnerable overall, they have yielded just 5.5 points per game on targets beyond 15 air yards (31st), which poses a test for Collins' deep-target role. Houston enters as 4.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 22.5 points (16th). Los Angeles hasn't had SCB Derwin James.
13. Matthew Golden (at NE) - 67.5 proj. receiving yards
14. Rashee Rice (vs. NYJ) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Rice is the WR21 on WR39 usage, a 19% target share and 6.3 targets per game in his four healthy games. He's finished between WR12 and WR32 in all of them, though he's running pretty pure in terms of efficiency with a sprinkling of broken plays. The good news for him is the Xavier Worthy threat has closed based on his tape and Travis Kelce's YAC greatness has stalled. Rice is back to being needed, even if Kenneth Walker III's presence is going to knock Rice down from his pre-2026 peak.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The matchup is a great one. The Jets have been particularly weak against shallow WRs, allowing the eighth-most production on throws within 10 air yards. Jalen Nailor snuck by with a WR20 finish last week, while role players Caleb Douglas (WR8) and Pop Douglas (WR10) balled out in the games prior. A monster 28.75-point team total has Rice's projection looking the best it has all year.
15. Luther Burden III (vs. TB) - 65.5 proj. receiving yards

Burden played three of 21 snaps in heavy personnel. When the Bears established a lead, they went away from 3-WR sets, which is partially explaining the massive splits between halves for Burden this season. He's the WR3 in yards per route in the first half and the WR61 in the second half. When Johnson hasn't isolated him on a first read, the results are worse. That's the reality of a physically dominant yet in-development player. Burden is the WR24 on WR7 usage in games with Caleb this year, so it's no reason to really panic. He's an upside WR2/3 despite the obvious inconsistency.
16. Parker Washington (at BAL) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

Washington is extremely volatile. On average, he's the WR20 on WR23 usage. The last time he bottomed out, Washington was the WR3 overall the following week. He's not doing anything wrong. In fact, he's the WR15 in yards per route.

This past week, the Jaguars had five explosives through the air. All of them were to TEs and RBs. That's the magic of Liam Coen's scheme, but when those plays are working and the Colts couldn't move the ball on the other side, then there aren't enough dropbacks to go around. Washington is arguably better in more difficult matchups.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The matchup against Baltimore offers a bounce-back opportunity, as the Ravens rank ninth in half PPR points allowed to WRs at 28.6 per game. Baltimore has struggled against intermediate passing in particular, ranking 10th in points allowed on targets between five and 20 air yards, where Washington has logged 30 targets this season. Jacksonville enters as 8.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 25.5 points (ninth).
17. George Pickens (at IND) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Pickens had his second-lowest usage of the season last week, despite an easy matchup with the Cardinals that even went to overtime. Pickens only played 10 of 28 snaps with more than one TE on the field, allowing Ryan Flournoy to score a red-zone touchdown in a 3-TE set. These are things on the margins that will prevent Pickens from reaching top-15 status while CeeDee Lamb is healthy. Pickens will need to win his difficult assignments as the static X receiver in 3-WR sets. Dak Prescott is talented enough for spike weeks, but the consistency will be painful. Pickens is the WR28 on WR18 usage this season. He's firmly a boom-bust WR2, and I'd understand the Cowboys listening to trade offers for his expiring contract now that they trust Flournoy.

Pickens will battle with Sauce Gardner on the boundary most likely, but the rest of the defense is so overmatched here. The Jaguars moved the ball at will last week with DT DeForest Buckner gone. A monster 28.75-point team total (second) keeps the Pickens' ceiling intact.
18. Michael Wilson (at SEA) - 48.5 proj. receiving yards

I guess I appreciate Wilson's game way more than everyone else. His style is similar to Puka Nacua, although Wilson tends to be a little more out of control compared to the All Pro. How they're used and how physical they are is nearly identical. There have been too many misses by the QBs and too many DPIs/drops to treat him as a set-and-forget WR1, but Wilson is the WR5 in expected half PPR points this season.

He's no longer competing with WRs Marvin Harrison Jr., Kendrick Bourne, Jalen Brooks or Reggie Virgil for targets, and both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight also went down with injuries in Week 8. Wilson ended that contest as the WR4 on WR1 overall usage (30.2 expected half PPR points). Have we reached too big to fail? I think so. I'm buying, assuming his two broken ribs aren't going to derail his own season.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The matchup is obviously daunting. The Seahawks have allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to WRs, and they've been elite at stopping big plays over the middle and down the field, where Wilson has done a chunk of his damage. The Cardinals only have a 14.5-point team total with Minshew walking into an impossible task. Spamming underneath targets to Wilson has to be a big part of the plan.
19. Jameson Williams (at MIA) - 52.5 proj. receiving yards
20. DJ Moore (at MIN) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Week 8 was extremely encouraging for Moore. He was the WR13 on WR9 usage, and the scheme choices were great. His TD came from the slot in the high red zone on a run-away route, which suits his game best down there. He had another slot crosser, too. They connected on a deep play-action post against Marlon Humphrey, and then tested the veteran safety on a slant from the 5-yard line. Moore is getting used like the most important player in the pass game, one that sits here over the past three years:
(Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The matchup is obviously horrific with the Vikings shutting down everyone, including the Lions’ pass game last week. They do really shut down TEs, however, so the Bills could lean on Moore and James Cook III a bit more than others have. Allen is also better equipped to deal with the pressure they bring than other statue quarterbacks. It's still a bad matchup, one worth knocking Moore down some, but I'm less sure Moore will be the one specifically hurt most by this.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)
21. Zay Flowers (vs. JAX) - 48.5 proj. receiving yards

Over the past two years, Flowers has averaged 11.6 half PPR points without Lamar Jackson. That does not include last week's goose egg, nor does it adjust for Tyler Huntley (turf toe) out for the season. Over the past month with backups, Flowers is the WR22 on WR23 usage and that's probably closer to his ceiling than his baseline with "Joe Fagnano" under center on a short week.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

Fagnano is a big statue QB who made more plays than I thought he did on tape. There was a ton of bad luck involved on his throws to Flowers, who had a drop on a potential YAC opportunity over the middle. Another pass to Flowers was knocked down by an EDGE and another third-down rep by Flowers resulted in him falling down instead of being a first-read target.
(Photo by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports)

The challenge with the matchup is the Jaguars have been very good at stopping the short pass, limiting production on throws to WRs under 10 air yards to a No. 29 ranking. Some of that is having Travis Hunter on these quick in-breakers, and that size matchup wouldn't make me feel great about Flowers here. Where they've been weaker is on deep throws, and we'll see if Fagnano can push the ball against these dynamic edge rushers. It's certainly asking for a lot. The Ravens have a sub-15.0 team total here. Flowers is a desperation WR2/3.

On tape, Diggs is playing this crafty slot/underneath role in ways as Travis Kelce plays it. He'll find soft spots in zone and out of structure. He's a clear red-zone threat with space getting tight. The Rams rank 26th in half PPR points allowed to WRs at 22.4 per game, and teams routinely tilt away from passing against them, as their 47% neutral pass rate allowed ranks 30th (third-lowest). articles.headline: Cucco locations in Kakariko Village in Ocarina of Time
keyFacts: A farmer in Kakariko Village asks players to locate and return seven escaped Cuccos in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
Players can find all seven chickens throughout the village, with some requiring specific actions like breaking boxes or using another Cucco to glide.
Returning all seven Cuccos to the farmer rewards the player with an empty bottle, which is a significant item in the game.
body: Finding The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's Kakariko Cucco locations seems like a chore too bothersome to deal with. A farmer lost her seven chickens, and she wants your help finding them and bringing them back to their little fenced-off area. She's got a very good reward for you, though, so the task is definitely worth your time, even if it isn't the most straightforward to complete.
Below, we show you where to find all the Kakariko Cucco locations in Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
Cucco locations in Kakariko Village in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake

The distressed farmer needs you to find seven escaped Cuccos, of which only a few are immediately visible. Inaccessible as a couple of the locations might seem, you can find all seven chickens during your first visit to Kakariko Village before setting foot in Dodongo Cavern — and you should. Your reward for bringing them safely home to roost is an empty bottle, and those are among the most important items in the game.

You can find the Cuccos in any order. We've just numbered them in the order we happened to run across them. Note that some of the birds wander from the location shown in these images, though they remain in the same general area.
Cucco #1 location
The first one is in the northern part of the village on a ledge near a home. This one wanders, so it might be in front of the house or behind it.
Cucco #2 location

The second Cucco managed to trap itself in a wooden box just to the south of the first one, nestled against the side of a house. Smack the box with your sword or roll into it to break it, and then take the chicken back home.
Cucco #3 location
Number three is wandering along the path that leads back to Hyrule Field in the western part of the village.
Cucco #4 location

Cucco number four is lazing around the construction site underneath the wooden scaffolding. There's a Gold Skulltula on the platform above it, too, so make sure to grab that after you take the Cucco home.
Cucco #5 location

The next one is on a pile of bricks in the south-central part of the village. You can get it down by firing a seed from your slingshot at it, which startles the poor Cucco and makes it fly down. Run after it, pick it up, and take it home. Despite your aggressive behavior, this single shot won't incite a Cucco mob to attack Link, as long as you don't keep hitting the bird.
Cucco #6 location

Finding the next Cucco requires the aid of another Cucco. It's behind the tall wooden fencing, and the only way to reach it is by climbing the steps in front of the windmill, holding a Cucco, and jumping. The Cucco flaps its wings so you glide, which gives you enough height to clear the top of the fence. Toss that Cucco back over, then grab the sixth Cucco and toss them over, too.
Cucco #7 location

Before you cross over the fence again, climb the ladder leading up the stone wall. The final Cucco is wandering around the windmill here. Speak to the farmer again after the final Cucco is returned, and she'll hand over your shiny new empty bottle.

articles.headline: No, the Chiefs aren't trading for Vikings star Justin Jefferson
keyFacts: A viral social media report claiming the Kansas City Chiefs are trading for Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson is false.
The report originated from an anonymous parody account on X and has no basis in reality.
The Chiefs are expected to pursue wide receiver upgrades before the trade deadline, but Jefferson is not a realistic target.
body: The Kansas City Chiefs are going to be buyers at the 2026 NFL trade deadline, and the one position they've been linked to more than anything else is wide receiver.

Players like Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. have emerged as realistic targets for the Chiefs, but they would surely love to find a way to get a true superstar in a deal. However, such a trade is not likely, even if they make a significant offer.

But on Thursday, November 5, @NFCNorthNewss shared on Twitter/x that the Chiefs were making a blockbuster trade for Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson. To put it as simply as possible: No, the Chiefs are not trading for Jefferson; this rumor is false.
No, the Chiefs are not trading for Justin Jefferson

"BREAKING: The Minnesota Vikings are finalizing a trade to send WR Justin Jefferson to the Kansas City Chiefs in exchange for a 2027 1st-round pick, as well as a 2nd-round pick in 2027 and 2028," @NFCNorthNewss shared on Twitter/x.

While there is a very real chance the Chiefs acquire a wide receiver, it would be stunning if it wound up being Jefferson. It would be on par with the Luka Doncic trade in the NBA made by the Los Angeles Lakers and the Dallas Mavericks.

While some fans might've gotten duped by this "reported" trade, it's a complete fabrication. No trade has been completed, and there's no chance a trade will actually be completed between the Chiefs and Vikings involving Jefferson.

Besides, the Vikings would likely ask for a lot more than that offer of one first-round pick and two second-round picks. If a trade actually happened, talks would start at two first-round picks and likely require the equivalent of a third first-rounder as well.
So, not only is this trade report a total lie, which should be expected coming from an anonymous parody account on Twitter/x, but it's not even a realistic fabricated trade either.

The Vikings didn't trade Jefferson to the Chiefs. This is a fake trade, which garnered over one million views and over 1,000 likes. It certainly got a lot of eyes on it, but it's not a real trade. The Chiefs will not be getting Justin Jefferson from the Vikings.

body: Devin Haney will return to boxing in a unification fight against Liam Paro in San Francisco on December 19.

The 27-year-old, born and raised in the San Francisco Bay Area, enters the December clash with a perfect 33-0 record and 15 knockouts to his name.
He was initially defeated by current WBC champion Ryan Garcia when the pair came to blows in New York in 2024, but the result was overturned to a no-contest when Garcia failed two drug tests.
This will be the first fight of Haney’s multi-fight partnership with streaming giant DAZN.
Haney inked an exclusive deal with DAZN last month, joining fellow boxing stars Anthony Joshua and Teofimo Lopez , who holds the fourth WBA belt at welterweight.
Dana White ‘s Zuffa Boxing had offered Haney a deal, which came with the stipulation that he would fight Shakur Stevenson , who has since left the promotion .

“Back home to the bay!” Haney wrote on X.
“Unified Champ Dec 19th InshaAllah… 34-0 #TheDream.”
Paro, meanwhile, won his IBF title with a unanimous decision win over Lewis Crocker in June.
The Australian has suffered just one defeat — a split decision to Richardson Hitchins in 2024 — in 29 professional fights, and the Haney fight marks just his third outing in the US.

articles.headline: The Best Thing I’ve Seen In The Ocarina Of Time Remake Is This Guy In Castle Town
keyFacts: A character in the Ocarina of Time remake features a beard that acts as a beacon to locate other bearded men in Hyrule.
The character serves as a narrative device to help players find Talon, who provides a horse for faster travel.
The character appeared in the original game but lacked the ability to track other bearded men.
body: Sometimes you meet a video game character that is your kindred spirit, separated from you by the unbreakable walls of your TV screen and gigabytes of code. I, like many people today, am playing through the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and a lot of the prettied-up N64 game is familiar to me as someone who played the game for months straight in elementary school. But as I entered Castle Town, the jubilant town square, I met a man who has a new role in the remake, and I need him to teach me his ways.

Thereâs a Dorito-shaped man in Ocarina of Timeâs remade Castle Town who has no real name, but is known as the Bearded Guy of Castle Town.Â He is tall, imposing, and has a regal-as-fuck âface maneâ that hangs down his face and onto his giant chest. Obviously, Nintendo knew they were making a new character for Zelda fans to thirst over like they do the Bombchu lady, but he is clearly catering toward a specific demographic of scruffy muscle gays. If I wasnât already drawn in by his design, I locked in when he told me that his beard acts as a âbeaconâ that can locate other bearded men throughout all of Hyrule.
Brother, what?Â

At first, I thought he was brand new to the remake because I didn’t remember a character occupying his role, but it turns out, he was there in the background, but wasn’t superpowered, or whatever he’s got going on. The game uses this gag as a way to tell you about Talon, the owner of Lon Lon Ranch that youâll meet later in the game, who also has a beard. Itâs a silly way for the game to point you in the direction of a side objective, one that will lead to you acquiring a horse to help you get across Hyrule more quickly than on foot. However, Iâm not even concerned about that. Why does my beard not give me the power to find other bearded men? Do you know how many places Iâve gone to in search of bearded men? Places I wouldnât go to with a gun! Whereâs this muscle gay firmware update? How long do I have to go to the gym before my beard gains wifi access and can directly connect to other bearded men without having to pay for a Scruff membership?
Well, until I find that out, at least I got this incredible image for my future dating profiles:

Pierre Sage was handed a much-needed lifeline as Crystal Palace snatched a dramatic late 1-1 draw against Hoffenheim in the Europa League, despite playing the final stages with 10 men following Adam Wharton's dismissal.
Palace arrived at Selhurst Park desperate for a response after three consecutive Premier League defeats had left them in the relegation zone, with growing questions over Sage's future as manager.

But their defensive vulnerabilities were exposed once again as Alexander Prass opened the scoring for Hoffenheim in the seventh minute, his effort squirming underneath Dean Henderson after the hosts were caught on the counter.

Sage's side showed some attacking promise but struggled to turn possession into clear-cut opportunities, while Hoffenheim looked dangerous whenever they broke forward.

But just when it looked as though another damaging defeat was inevitable, Daichi Kamada rescued a point in stoppage time. Yeremy Pino delivered a cross into the area, Tyrick Mitchell nodded the ball down and Kamada finished through the goalkeeper's legs to spark relief around Selhurst Park and give Sage a precious moment of respite.

The draw leaves Palace with plenty to address, particularly defensively, but the manner of their late equaliser could prove significant for a manager whose position has come under increasing scrutiny. Sage will breathe easier, although this was hardly a performance to silence his critics ahead of Sunday's Premier League meeting with Liverpool, live on Sky Sports.

body: TikTok just released a standalone Shop app, but it's not in America just yet

articles.headline: Russell to have 'deep, deep look in mirror'
keyFacts: Mercedes driver George Russell plans to reflect on his performance after a disappointing 2026 season.
Russell attributed his poor results to technical issues occurring in 14 of the 20 races this season.
The driver finished sixth in Mexico City after a power loss and a collision, dropping him to fourth in the championship standings.
body: - Published
George Russell says he plans to have a "deep, deep look in the mirror" to work out how he can improve after a disappointing 2026 season.

The Mercedes driver has watched team-mate Kimi Antonelli dominate on his way to becoming the youngest Formula 1 champion in history, while Russell has won only three races compared with the Italian's nine, despite starting the year as championship favourite.
Russell says luck has not been on his side, but wants to ensure he does everything he can to understand why he has lacked pace.
The Briton said: "It wasn't meant to be this season but you also need to look at yourself in the mirror and think: 'What could I have done better'?
"Is all of the misfortune truly misfortune? Or is it actually things in our control that could have been better?
"So you need to just have a deep, deep look in the mirror and pick yourself up again and go from there."
Russell said he and his team had analysed the season so far and worked out that he has had a trouble-free run in only six of this season's 20 races.
"These issues constantly keep popping up but unfortunately this always seems like it's on my side of the garage," he said.
"We concluded we've only had six races from the 20 where we've had a clean weekend. So to think 14 of those weekends have had issues is unbelievable.
"We need to look to understand why that is, if there's something we are overlooking or if it's just pure misfortune. At the moment it does seem like it's more misfortune than anything.
"In a normal season you might have two weekends or three weekends where there are issues. We've had three quarters of this season and that has been incredibly unfortunate."

He said it was the fact that he had been struck by another technical glitch that made him skip his media duties after last weekend's Mexico City race, rather than the fact Antonelli had just won the title.
Russell, who started second to Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari, had a loss of power on the run to the first corner when the electrical part of the power-unit did not reply properly.

He was swamped by the field, and then collided with Isack Hadjar's Red Bull at Turn Six, earning himself a 10-second penalty. He finished sixth and dropped from second to fourth in the drivers' championship, behind Antonelli, Max Verstappen and Hamilton.
"In racing you always pick yourself back up and for me the best way to pick myself back up was getting out of there," Russell said on media day for this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

"It was as simple as that, really. I was just very upset with missing out on the chance of a good result because the championship for me was already over but I just couldn't believe how things had panned out again.
"In that moment, yeah, I just wanted to get out of there.
"I think I'm 99% of the time a true professional and I try not to spit my dummy out, but sometimes missing out on doing the press â OK, it's not ideal but not the end of the world.
"Moments like that you don't really want to deal with it."

articles.headline: Los Angeles and Washington, DC, go down the path of socialism
keyFacts: Voters in Los Angeles elected Democratic Socialists of America member Nithya Raman over Mayor Karen Bass.

body: Voters in Los Angeles and Washington, D.C., have added their cities to the ranks of American cities run by socialists . You can only hope that those voters get everything they voted for, just as voters in other socialist-run cities have before them.

Los Angeles voters chose to dump Mayor Karen Bass, herself a sympathizer of Cuba’s communist regime, in favor of Democratic Socialists of America member Nithya Raman. Raman is just as guilty of the city’s failures as Bass, having served on the city council, and the biggest difference between the two is that Raman is more accepting of unsanitary, dangerous homeless encampments popping up around the city.
THE SOCIALIST PLAYBOOK CRUSHES SMALL BUSINESSES

Meanwhile, voters in Washington, D.C., elected Janeese Lewis George , a socialist who has promised more spending despite the city already facing a $680 million budget gap. Lewis George is also a DSA member who sat on her city’s council and has cheered the hobbyist protesters in Minnesota, stating , “Imagine what it would be like to have a Mayor who was helping to lead the resistance.” Lewis George wants the National Guard members who have helped drive down the district’s crime to be taken off the streets.

Other cities have already thrown themselves to the socialist wolves, with predictable results. Chicago elected Brandon Johnson in 2023, a socialist in all but the label he gives himself. His election followed a similar path to Raman’s, with voters choosing the more left-wing candidate to replace the already very far-left incumbent (in this case, Lori Lightfoot). Chicago’s schools are failing , the city has no grasp on its rampant crime problem, and city leaders have still failed to handle the budget crisis they have been wrestling with for years. As of October, Johnson had an approval rating of 22%, with his disapproval sitting at 53%.
WHY MAMDANI DOESN’T CARE ABOUT SOCIALISM’S GRIM RECORD

Seattle elected socialist Katie Wilson in 2025, another far-left candidate replacing the left-wing incumbent. With Seattle’s downtown hollowed out and residents wanting to move out because of taxes and a lack of affordability, Wilson came into office promising higher taxes, more rent control, and more tolerance for homeless encampments. Wilson even came into office promoting a boycott of Starbucks, the iconic Washington state company that employs thousands of Seattle residents and provides the city with a large chunk of tax revenue.

Combine that with New York City socialist Mayor Zohran Mamdani pushing ahead with his tax and rent control policies that will drive more residents out of the Big Apple, and you have a who’s who of major American cities under the thumb of socialist policies that have a proven track record of failure. Washington, D.C., and Los Angeles were both failing cities already, but Chicago has shown that it can always get worse. Now, those cities join the rest on the socialist trajectory, and no one will be able to argue that those voters aren’t getting exactly what they voted for.

articles.headline: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar
keyFacts: Meta announced on Thursday that the Muse Voice video chatting feature is now available to all U.S. users.
The feature uses new AI models to power a customizable, animated digital avatar that interacts with users during live conversations.
Meta stated that the real-time conversations will later expand to AI Glasses and the upcoming Muse Charm hardware device.
body: Muse Voice, a feature that lets users call and video chat with Meta’s consumer AI agent, Muse, is now available to everyone in the U.S., the company announced on Thursday.

First introduced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September, the video chatting feature involves new AI models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology, which help power the digital avatar that chats with the user.

While other AI competitors offer voice chat features, Meta’s Muse offers a cute, animated avatar (nicknamed Jolly), which users interact with as they ask questions or request tasks to be handled on their behalf. Users can also customize the avatar as they choose, changing it to something that looks more like a person, animal, or some other character.

The company believes that anthropomorphizing Muse in this way could make consumers feel more connected to their AI agent — a connection that could grow even stronger as they begin to engage in live conversations with it.
As the Muse avatar speaks, Meta says it will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that match the tone of the conversation.

The news of the rollout was announced via blog post and on X by Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, who shared a demo of his Muse in action. The video saw Wang joking around, referencing his love of posting memes on X, which he told his Muse may have gotten him in trouble with his boss. His Muse, a fluffy white dog, responds with a suggestion to add disclaimers to those memes that could be misinterpreted as Meta endorsing anything risque. (Ha!)

The added support for video chats and calls comes just before Meta’s plan to launch a Tamagotchi-like wearable device for its Muse AI agent before year-end. When the device arrives, the digital avatar will appear on its small screen, letting users talk to the agent, which can then reply or carry out tasks for them.
Meta says the real-time conversations are supported on mobile, web, and Mac and will later come to its AI Glasses and the upcoming “Muse Charm” hardware device.

articles.headline: US elections 2026 live: Democrats flip four more House seats as Republicans trade blame for brutal midterms losses
keyFacts: Democrats flipped four more House seats to strengthen their new lower chamber majority with 247 total seats.
